newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa seen headed for 10,300pta resistance.
newsitem.headline: Endesa seen headed for 10,300pta resistance.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Endesa soared again on Wednesday, heading for its next chart resistance around 10,300 pesetas in the short term, dealers said.
Endesa shares have risen 11 percent percent since April 14 after a period of underperformance. They hit an all-time high of 10,350 pesetas on January 22.
At 1025 GMT today it was outperforming again, adding 190 pesetas, 1.92 percent, to 10,100. The Ibex-35 blue chip index was rising just 1.0 percent to 5,787.74.
Analysts linked the change in sentiment to information from the firm regarding plans to cut costs and increase dividends, given to analysts and investors.

"It was about time Endesa started to make presentations. It has a latent value which is not reflected, and people need to know that the protocol doesn't represent any risk for the company," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage in Madrid.
"We're expecting the share price to continue to react underpinned by the fact that they're making their presentations to institutional investors rather than analysts," he added.
He set a short-term target price at 10,500 pesetas, and a 12-month objective at 11,500-12,000 pesetas.

In December, electricity companies agreed a framework for sector liberalisation. This will reduce Endesa's annual income but should increase efficiency savings or capital gains, according to the Energy Department.

A utilities analyst at a Spanish bank said the presentations "were valued very positively as it provided a clear message from the new management team and assured the market that growth possibilities continue to exist in the new sector scenario."
"..the company continues to have maximising shareholder value as its main priority," he said.
Endesa said on Friday it would cut costs aggressively, and would increase the diversity of its business.
Analysts added that fears of share price weakness if the state sells more of Endesa than was originally planned this year seem to have dissipated.
State holding company SEPI still owns 67 percent of the firm, with the next privatisation due in the autumn.
